compound.name: methyl cinnamate
compound.one_liner: Fruity-balsamic ester that gives 'Cinnamon' basil its name: 24.7 % of volatiles, second to linalool.

identity.note: (E)-isomer record; the Cinnamon-basil paper reports (E)-methyl cinnamate.

occurrences.source_citation: Majdi C, Pereira C, Dias MI, et al. (2020) Phytochemical characterization and bioactive properties of cinnamon basil (Ocimum basilicum cv. 'Cinnamon') and lemon basil (Ocimum × citriodorum). Antioxidants 9(5):369
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: Value from paper: in O. basilicum cv. 'Cinnamon', (E)-methyl cinnamate 'presented also a very high amount (24.7%)', second to linalool. Duke: METHYL-CINNAMATE Plant 1-2800 ppm. | Basis as recorded: % of total volatiles

processing_stability.volatility: steam-volatile: recovered in hydro/steam-distilled essential oil (see occurrence sources)
processing_stability.note: Solubility and heat-stability values not sourced in this pass.

compound.teaching_note: 'Cinnamon' basil does not contain cinnamon's cinnamaldehyde; its note comes from methyl cinnamate, and even there linalool is the larger component [19].
gaps: Pharmacology, absorption and safety not researched.
No human evidence for the isolated compound found in this pass.
Plant part for the 24.7 % value not re-confirmed.
